basis: Extramedullary tumour of immature myeloid blood cells; anatomical sites vary, with no additional organ consistently affected.
Thyroid hormone deficiency; symptoms and uncommon severe complications do not establish additional organ damage across this umbrella.
Adipocytic soft-tissue sarcoma, generally arising in connective tissues; no specific visceral site is intrinsic to this histological variant.
Destructive glomerular inflammation with crescents and rapidly declining renal function; underlying mechanisms are predominantly immune-mediated.
Defined by corpus callosum maldevelopment and deficient pituitary hormone production.
Maternal blocking autoantibodies cause transient thyroid hormone deficiency; constipation, dry skin and hyporeflexia do not establish lasting organ damage.
Nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia; elevated ferritin alone does not establish damaging iron deposition in other organs.
Autoimmune inflammatory muscle and skin disease; ILD is uncommon in this antibody subtype, and dysphagia generally reflects the myopathy.
Skeletal muscle channelopathy causing myotonia; potassium sensitivity does not constitute a systemic metabolic disorder.
Autoinflammation with chronic meningitis and defining arthropathy; hearing loss 80-99%; uveitis 80-99% and defining skin disease omitted because of four-axis cap.
Hereditary nephropathy with sensorineural deafness and characteristic ocular defects; lenticonus and retinal hemorrhage are frequent HPO findings, unlike harmless retinal flecks.
Autosomal dominant nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss.
B-cell lymphoma, usually confined to peripheral lymph nodes; splenic, hepatic and marrow involvement are minority findings.
The specified syndrome comprises granulomatous arterial inflammation and juvenile inflammatory polyarthritis; no evidence supports additional organs.
Senior-Loken syndrome combines nephronophthisis with retinal dystrophy; supplied findings include kidney failure in 21/21 and rod-cone dystrophy in 7/21.
Inherited pyrophosphate metabolism defect causes arterial calcification and stenosis; renal artery disease is vascular, and rickets is occasional in supplied HPO.
Inborn phospholipid-remodelling disorder with neurologic dysfunction; deafness occurs in about 80% of the predominant MEGDEL phenotype; milder presentations vary.
Hereditary abnormal apolipoprotein metabolism produces predominantly renal amyloid deposition and progressive nephropathy; other damaging sites are not established as common.
Neoplasm of the ovaries or fallopian tubes; reproductive organs have no axis.
Blistering skin disease umbrella with genetic, infectious, immune and other causes; no single mechanism or extracutaneous organ applies across the group.
Inflammation of kidney tissue; the broad category includes multiple causes and does not uniformly establish infection or an immune-mediated mechanism.
Inflammation of the cornea; infectious, immune, traumatic and other causes prevent assigning a uniform mechanism axis.
Renal malformations are a major syndromic component in approximately 30-40%, supported by frequent HPO annotation; uterovaginal aplasia has no axis; skeletal defects are less common.
Intellectual disability and global developmental delay define the disorder; other potentially damaging organ findings occur in fewer than 30%.
Borderline serous epithelial neoplasm arising in the ovary, a reproductive organ outside the axes; no common direct damage to another organ is established.
